If I understand your query correctly, you are asking for a non-fiction story in which the protagonist is depicted one way (e.g. a hero) but the story is incomplete and the public later learns about the hero’s fall from grace.

If that’s the case, the first person who comes to mind is Lance Armstrong and his biography, “It’s not about the bike” published in 2000 roughly a dozen years before he was found to have taken (PEDs) performance enhancing drugs.

There is also “The Autobiography of Howard Hughes”, written by Yale educated Clifford Irving as a sort of “as told to” account of the eccentric and reclusive billionaire. It was later discovered that Irving had fabricated the entire story and he went to jail for it.

I guess you could also look at “Fatherhood” by Bill Cosby in light of what we know about him today.

It seems like these kind of stories are common place among athletes and entertainers but I’m not as familiar with nonfiction books written about such figures as Tiger Woods and Aaron Hernandez.

Hope this helps a little.
